h1: Why hire a digital agency instead of building a team
metaTitle: Why Hire a Digital Agency? The Honest Case
metaDescription: Why hire a digital agency instead of building in-house? Run the real INR maths on four salaries plus tools, and see three cases where in-house wins.
answer: Hire a digital agency when you need four skills — paid media, SEO, content and design — and can't justify four salaries. Four junior-to-mid hires in an Indian metro cost roughly ₹2,00,000–₹3,50,000 a month in salary alone, before tools, recruitment and ramp-up. A retainer buys the same coverage as variable cost.
takeaways: The comparison isn't one salary versus one retainer. It's **four salaries plus tools plus three months of hiring** versus one invoice you can stop.
Agencies win on breadth and speed to competence. In-house wins on depth, context and anything that has to happen daily.
Three situations genuinely favour in-house: one dominant channel, deep product context, and high-volume repeatable output.
The hybrid almost always beats both — one senior in-house owner of the number, agency hands underneath.

sections.h2: The arithmetic nobody puts in the pitch deck
body: Most founders compare a ₹1,00,000 retainer to one ₹60,000 hire and conclude the agency is expensive. That's the wrong comparison. To cover what a mid-sized retainer covers, you need four people, and none of them can do the other three's jobs.

Here's the salary line for an Indian metro. Treat these as broad market bands, not quotes — they vary by city, sector and how badly you need someone to start next week, and they move faster than any published survey keeps up with. Tier-2 cities typically run 30–40% below these.

bullets: **Tools**: a rank tracker and backlink suite, a scheduler, design software, stock, call tracking. Realistically ₹15,000–₹40,000 a month for a small team, and the good SEO suites are dollar-priced.
**Recruitment**: an agency recruiter in India commonly charges 8.33% of annual CTC. Four hires is a real number, and that's before your own time in interviews.
**Ramp**: two to three months to fill each seat, then 60–90 days before anyone is useful. You're paying full salary throughout.
**Management**: somebody senior has to brief, review and unblock four people. If that's you, price your own hours honestly.

callout.title: The number that actually matters
callout.body: Fully loaded, a four-person in-house team lands somewhere around ₹2,00,000–₹3,50,000 a month in year one, and it's fixed cost. A ₹99,000–₹1,75,000 retainer covers similar ground and stops with 30 days' notice. That flexibility is most of what you're paying for. Full retainer bands sit in [what a digital marketing agency costs in India](/cost/digital-marketing-agency-cost-india).

sections.h2: Speed to competence, which is the real product
body: Money aside, the thing an agency actually sells is a shorter distance to knowing what to do. A team that has run forty accounts in your category has already made the mistakes you're about to pay for: the migration that dropped 40% of traffic, the campaign structure that burned budget on brand terms, the content plan aimed at keywords nobody buys from.
That pattern library is real and it's genuinely hard to replicate in-house, because one company only sees one dataset. Your first in-house hire learns on your money and your calendar.

The honest counterweight: an agency's pattern library also makes it lazy. Templates are efficient right up until your business is the exception. Ask any agency what they'd do differently for you than for their last client in your sector — if the answer is thin, you're buying the template.

sections.h2: Three cases where in-house genuinely wins
body: We lose these arguments regularly and we should. If you're in one of these three, don't hire us or anyone like us.

subs.h3: One channel dominates and it's operationally heavy
body: If 80% of revenue comes from paid media and you're spending well into seven figures a month, percentage-of-spend fees stop making sense fast. At 12% of ₹30,00,000 in monthly spend you're paying ₹3,60,000 for work an in-house buyer plus a creative could run. The same logic applies to marketplace-led businesses where somebody has to touch listings every single day.

subs.h3: The product takes months to understand
body: Deep B2B, regulated categories, complex engineering products. If a writer needs six months of context before producing anything credible, agency turnover will kill you — you'll re-onboard three times before anything good ships. Hire one person who stays.

A D2C brand shipping thirty creative variants a week does not want a briefing loop and an approval queue in between. Once the work is defined and constant, in-house is cheaper per unit and considerably faster. Agencies are expensive per unit and good at the parts that keep changing.
The setup that works most often isn't either/or. It's one senior in-house marketer who owns the number, with agency hands doing the volume underneath.

The in-house owner holds context, prioritises, kills bad ideas fast, and cares about the outcome the way only someone with equity or a job title on the line does. The agency brings the four disciplines, the tools and the pattern library without four salaries. It also means somebody internal can read an SEO report critically, which is the difference between managing an agency and being managed by one.

One rule: the owner must be senior enough to say no. A junior coordinator with an agency to manage becomes a message-relay service, and the agency ends up setting its own homework. Our own bundles are built for exactly this shape — see the [pricing page](/pricing) for what each one covers.

callout.title: Where the guarantee fits
callout.body: We freeze your trailing-90-day qualified leads from organic search on day one and keep working free if we haven't beaten that number in 90 days. It's a promise against your own starting line, never a promised ranking position. It also gives your in-house owner something specific to hold us to.

sections.h2: How to avoid paying for both at once
body: The expensive failure mode isn't hiring an agency or hiring in-house. It's running both without dividing the work, then paying twice for the same output while each side assumes the other has it covered.
numbered: **Write a one-page split.** Every activity — keyword research, publishing, link outreach, ad creative, reporting — gets exactly one owner's name against it. One page, reviewed quarterly.
**Audit the tool stack once.** Agencies bill tools into the retainer and in-house teams buy their own. Two rank trackers and two analytics dashboards is a common, silly ₹20,000 a month.
**Have one report, not two.** If both sides report separately you'll spend meetings reconciling numbers instead of deciding anything. Agree the source of truth on day one.

**Plan the taper deliberately.** If in-house is the destination, say so at the start and write a handover into the contract — documentation, tool transfer, a training window. Read [when to bring SEO in-house](/journal/when-to-bring-seo-in-house) before you set the date.
**Re-run the maths every six months.** Retainers get renewed on autopilot. Salaries don't. Whichever side you started on, the answer changes as you grow.

faqs.q: Is a digital agency cheaper than hiring in-house?
faqs.a: For breadth, usually yes. Four junior-to-mid metro hires run roughly ₹1,50,000–₹3,05,000 a month in salary before tools, recruitment fees and three months of ramp. A retainer covering the same disciplines is variable cost you can stop with 30 days' notice. For one channel at high volume, in-house wins.

faqs.q: How long before a digital agency pays for itself?
faqs.a: Paid media can show a read in weeks because the feedback loop is short. Organic channels take three to six months for real movement and six to twelve to compound. Budget twelve months of retainer before you judge SEO, and if you can't fund twelve, spend the money on a shorter-payback channel.

faqs.q: Can I hire an agency and an in-house marketer at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's usually the strongest setup — provided the in-house person is senior enough to own the number and say no. What fails is a junior coordinator relaying messages, because then the agency sets its own priorities and nobody internal can tell whether the work was any good.

faqs.q: What size of business should hire a digital agency?
faqs.a: Less about size, more about channel count and cash. If two or more channels need running properly and you can fund twelve months without flinching, an agency is efficient. If one channel drives everything and it's simple, a freelancer or your own two hours a week generally beats a thin retainer.

faqs.q: What do I lose by outsourcing marketing?
faqs.a: Context and continuity. An agency will never know your product like someone who sits in your sales calls, and staff churn resets some of that. Offset it by keeping assets in your name, insisting on documentation you can read, and having one internal person who genuinely understands the work.
